lessons.title: Pure Functions & Eliminating Side Effects
lessons.description: A pure function always returns the same output for the same input and has no side effects.

sections.heading: What is a pure function?
paragraphs: A pure function is predictable: given the same inputs, it always returns the same output and never modifies anything outside itself. Pure functions are the building blocks of reliable, testable code.
list: No side effects: no modifying globals, no DOM changes, no network calls
No reading external state: no global variables, no Math.random()
Easy to test, debug, and compose

codeExamples.heading: Pure vs impure functions
explanation: Pure functions depend only on their arguments — no surprises.
Impure functions read or modify external state, making behavior unpredictable.
Pure functions are trivial to test: just call and check the return value.
In FP, you pass data into functions and get new data back — no mutations.

practice.task: Convert an impure function that reads from a global variable into a pure function that takes all needed values as parameters.
hints: Identify every external variable the function reads.
Add those values as function parameters.
Remove any mutations — return new values instead.

keyTakeaways: Pure functions always return the same output for the same input.
No side effects: they don't modify external state or read global variables.
They're easy to test, reason about, and compose into larger programs.
Make functions pure whenever possible — use side effects only at the edges of your program.
lessons.challenge: Write 3 pure functions for a shopping cart: addItem, removeItem, and calculateTotal. All should return new values without mutating the original data.

lessons.title: Immutability Patterns in Application State
lessons.description: Instead of modifying data, create new copies with the changes — this prevents bugs in complex applications.

sections.heading: Why immutability?
paragraphs: When you mutate data, every function that touches it could potentially change it. Immutability means creating new values instead of modifying existing ones — this eliminates an entire class of bugs.
list: Never modify objects or arrays directly — create new ones
Use spread operator ... to copy and update
Use Object.freeze() to enforce immutability at runtime
React, Redux and many frameworks depend on immutability

codeExamples.heading: Immutable patterns
explanation: Spread ... creates a shallow copy of the object/array.
For objects, override properties after spreading: {...obj, newProp: val}.
For arrays, use filter() to remove, map() to update, ... to add.
The original data is never modified — all operations return new values.

practice.task: Given an array of users, write immutable operations to: add a new user, update a user's name, and remove a user by ID. Each operation should return a new array.

keyTakeaways: Immutability means creating new values instead of modifying existing ones.
Use spread ... to create shallow copies of objects and arrays.
Array methods like map(), filter() and reduce() return new arrays.
Immutability prevents accidental mutations and makes state changes predictable.
lessons.challenge: Build a todo list with immutable state management: add, toggle, remove, and edit — all returning new arrays.

lessons.title: Higher-Order Functions & Currying Patterns
lessons.description: Functions that accept or return other functions — the backbone of functional programming.

sections.heading: Higher-order functions
paragraphs: A higher-order function either takes a function as an argument or returns a function. Array methods like map(), filter(), and reduce() are all higher-order functions.
list: Accept a function as a parameter: map(fn), filter(fn)
Return a function: function multiply(n) { return (x) => x * n; }
Enable abstracting over behavior — pass different operations to the same function

sections.heading: Currying
list: Currying transforms a function that takes multiple args into a chain of functions each taking one arg
Useful for creating specialized functions from general ones
Common in functional programming and libraries like Redux

codeExamples.heading: Higher-order functions and currying
explanation: repeat takes a function and calls it multiple times — higher-order pattern.
multiply(2) returns a new function that doubles any input — currying.
Currying creates specialized functions from general ones.
This pattern makes code composable and reusable.

practice.task: Write a curried format Currency function: formatCurrency("USD")(100) returns "$100.00", formatCurrency("EUR")(100) returns "€100.00".
hints: Outer function takes the currency symbol.
Return the formatted string using the captured symbol.

keyTakeaways: Higher-order functions take or return functions — enabling behavior abstraction.
Currying transforms multi-argument functions into chains of single-argument functions.
Curried functions create specialized versions from general ones.
These patterns make code composable, reusable and declarative.
lessons.challenge: Write a generic createFilter(predicate) curried function that returns a filter function. Use it to create filters for even numbers, strings starting with 'a', and objects with price under 10.

lessons.title: Function Composition & Pipeline Concepts
lessons.description: Combine small functions into larger ones by chaining them together — like assembling Lego blocks.

sections.heading: Function composition
paragraphs: Composition is building complex operations by combining simple functions. The output of one function becomes the input of the next. This creates readable, maintainable code.
list: Each function does one thing well
The composed function describes the flow of data

codeExamples.heading: Compose and pipe utilities
explanation: compose applies functions right to left: round(applyDiscount(addTax(100))).
pipe applies functions left to right: addTax → applyDiscount → round.
Each small function is pure and does one thing.
The composed function reads like a data pipeline.

practice.task: Create pipe functions for text processing: trim, lowercase, and replace spaces with dashes. Pipe them together to convert "  Hello World  " to "hello-world".

keyTakeaways: Function composition combines small functions into larger ones.
Each function should be pure and do one thing well.
Composed functions describe data flow as a readable pipeline.
lessons.challenge: Build a data pipeline that takes an array of numbers, filters evens, doubles them, and sums the result — all composed from individual pure functions.
